subject: Failover grace-period carveout request and recovery-window plan for NovusPay
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops@novuspay.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Failover grace-period carveout request and recovery-window plan for NovusPay

Hi Diego / NovusPay ops team,

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. As discussed, NovusPay's routing and customer session consistency requirements mean the standard multi-region switchover assumption (transparent instant cutover) creates a brief period where your edge sessions may observe elevated tail latency. To support your production launch timeline we can propose a temporary carveout to the standard multi-region SLA that explicitly defines a short failover "grace period" and acceptance criteria.

High-level proposal (draft):
- Grace period: up to 12 minutes from primary-region failure detection to full traffic stabilization in the standby region (target RTO window).
- Recovery fidelity (RPO): prefix/KV-cache best-effort with documented cache-warm policies; expected message loss window <= 2 minutes for non-idempotent streams.
- Triggers: automatic routing failover on region health threshold + manual confirm button for momentary network anomalies.
- Operational conditions: NovusPay agrees to run an initial joint DR runbook test within 30 days and a quarterly tabletop thereafter.

I've attached a short analysis that models traffic cutover profiles and a draft SLA addendum with proposed redlines (recovery-analysis-novuspay.pdf / novuspay-sla-addendum-v1.docx).

Request: can you confirm whether NovusPay is willing to accept the 12-minute grace window and the associated acceptance criteria so we can route to legal and infra for final approval? If you prefer a shorter window (e.g., 8 minutes) we'll surface the corresponding operational and cost impacts.

Next steps I recommend from our side:
- Internal infra review (Markus) to confirm warm-standby sizing and cache-warm timelines.
- Product/ops to publish the joint runbook and monitoring hooks.
- Sign SLA addendum via DocuSign after legal review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the attached timing diagrams.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: recovery-analysis-novuspay.pdf, novuspay-sla-addendum-v1.docx, failover-timing-model.xlsx
From: Diego Fernández <diego@novuspay.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Sana Iqbal <sana.iqbal@novuspay.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2028 10:32:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Failover grace-period carveout request and recovery-window plan for NovusPay

Hi Aisha — thanks for the writeup and the attachments. Couple of immediate questions from our side: 

1) The 12-minute grace window: can you break that down into detection + orchestration + traffic drain times? NovusPay's payment routing has a 5-minute session affinity window we can't violate without customer impact.
2) Cache warming: what controls do we have to avoid duplicate deliveries during the warmup period? We need an explicit strategy for de-duping or idempotency guarantees for charge requests.
3) Will Redwood provide dedicated warm standby capacity in eu-west-1 or is this expected to be shared? If shared, we'll need stronger SLA credit language.

Also: we will need engineering contact details for the joint DR runbook test and a proposed date range (we favor Aug 6–10).

Diego
Director, Infrastructure — NovusPay

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernández <diego@novuspay.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Failover grace-period carveout request and recovery-window plan for NovusPay

Hi Diego — great questions. Quick answers below and a short ops checklist so we can get internal signoff.

Breakdown of the 12-minute window (typical timeline):
- Failure detection and health verification: 0–90s (automated monitoring + cross-region heartbeat checks)
- Routing orchestration and DNS TTL propagation handoff: ~2–4 minutes (we use low TTLs and a staged traffic shift to avoid global churn)
- Cache warm and session rehydration: 6–8 minutes (depends on the working set; our model for NovusPay indicates ~6.5 minutes median under current traffic; see failover-timing-model.xlsx)
- Final stabilization and monitoring confirmation: remainder to 12 minutes.

Cache/dedup strategy: 
- We recommend a short-lived idempotency token on charge requests and an at-least-once delivery model with de-dupe at application layer. For non-idempotent endpoints, we can enable request buffering during handoff and forward in-order once the KV cache has rehydrated. That reduces duplicate charge risk but increases RTO by ~90s in our tests.

Warm standby capacity: 
- For the carveout to hold we recommend NovusPay provision Dedicated shard capacity in eu-west-1 (reserved) for a six-month term. If you prefer shared capacity, we will require additional SLA credit language for priority capacity and preemption protections; that will change pricing.

Proposed runbook/test window: Aug 8 (preferred) — ops contacts below for scheduling and runbook items.

Ops checklist for internal signoff (action owners in parens):
- Warm-standby sizing confirmation + cost delta (Markus).
- SLA addendum legal review for credit & liability language (Marissa).
- Runbook, monitoring hooks, and post-test metrics (Aisha / NovusPay ops).

If this looks acceptable I'll ask legal to put a first-pass redline in DocuSign and we can aim to run the DR test August 8.

Best,
Aisha

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2028 14:12:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Failover grace-period carveout request and recovery-window plan for NovusPay

Aisha — reviewed the attachments and the timing model. My summary and caveats below.

Summary: we can support a 12-minute operational window if NovusPay agrees to either (A) reserved dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 sized at ~0.6x traffic (to allow for KV cache population) or (B) a shared-warm-standby but with priority preemption language and a 15% cost uplift. Without dedicated capacity the median cache-warm moves from ~6.5 minutes to ~9–10 minutes in noisy periods.

Caveats / asks for commercial/legal: 
- Legal: need to include a limited SLA credit schedule tied to a well-defined detection window and an explicit list of exclusion events (DDOS/failure with simultaneous upstream DNS issues). (Marissa: please draft redline example)
- Engineering: require access to NovusPay's session affinity and idempotency token schema for in-order replay testing during the DR run.
- Metrics: we must collect the post-run transient error histogram and token duplication counts; if duplication >0.1% we won't certify the shorter RPO.

If NovusPay signs up for the dedicated shard for six months we can ship the SLA addendum with the 12-minute target and include a one-time onboarding fee to cover pre-warm cache seeding.

Markus
Director, Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference

Diego — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Markus and Marissa's notes, here are the agreed next steps and the specific asks so we can finalize the addendum: 

1) Commercial & capacity decision (NovusPay): dedicated eu-west-1 shard for six months OR accept shared standby with 15% uplift. Please reply with which option by COB Wed Jul 26.
2) Engineering artifacts (NovusPay): session affinity TTLs, idempotency token format, and a sandbox endpoint for replay tests (due Jul 29).
3) DR run: Aug 8 — Redwood infra will lead the drill, NovusPay ops to provide 2 SREs for the runbook.
4) Legal: Marissa will circulate a DocuSign link for the SLA addendum v1 with the reserved-capacity and credit clauses baked in.

I attached the SLA addendum draft to this message (novuspay-sla-addendum-v1.docx). Please confirm acceptance of the dedicated shard option and we will issue the DocuSign envelope today.

If you prefer a shorter grace window we can evaluate an 8-minute target but you'll see an increase to the onboarding fee and a small monthly premium to cover increased warm-standby sizing.

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing.

Best,
Aisha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
